Closing a Connections panel clears parent's filter and highlightedRefs; after splice, a following Connections/compare panel is closed too.
Escape in a panel closes it (see keyboard).

name: Citation click opens cited text
summary: Clicking a citation opens the cited text in an adjacent panel (or replaces in mobile).
details: handleCitationClick(n,citationRef,textRef,replace,currVersions) (1077-1088): closes panel n+1 if replace or if it is Connections; highlights textRef in panel n; opens citation after n with scrollToHighlighted:!!replace.
Single-panel mode: ReaderPanel calls showBaseText instead (ReaderPanel.jsx:187-193).

VERIFIED 2026-10-06 on sefaria.org (scripts/probes/multipanel-probe*.mjs, scripts/parity-panels.mjs): a citation closes whatever is next to its panel — the panel's sidebar, or else the next panel even when the reader opened it — makes the verse holding the citation current, and opens the cited text right after: [Ramban on Genesis 1:1, Exodus 1] → citation Exodus 12:2 → /Ramban_on_Genesis.1.1.1?lang=bi&p2=Exodus.12.2&lang2=bi&aliyot2=0; a second citation replaces the first. OWNER DECISION: exactly as sefaria.org. BUILT (TextPanel onCitationClick); parity-panels equal.

name: Search/sidebar result navigation in panels
summary: Search results clicked inside side panels land in the right panel.
details: handleCompareSearchClick(n,...) replaces that panel for non-first panels (1102-1105,2452).
handleSidebarSearchClick(n,ref) replaces master panel (n-1) with highlight, scrollToHighlighted and showHighlight (1106-1116).

name: Connection filter state management
summary: Selecting a commentator/category filter updates sidebar mode and remembers recent filters.
details: setConnectionsFilter(n,filter,updateRecent) (1887-1910): moves filter to front of recentFilters (deduped via toggle); mode 'EssayList' if filter has suffix '|Essay' else 'TextList'; no filter -> 'ConnectionsList'; mirrors filter/recentFilters onto base panel.
setSideScrollPosition(n,pos) remembers sidebar scroll (1911-1915).
setConnectionsCategory sets filter for link dots and switches to 'ConnectionsList'; setWebPagesFilter -> 'WebPagesList'; editNote -> 'Edit Note' (ReaderPanel).

name: Version filter state in sidebar
summary: Choosing a translation/version in the sidebar tracks recent version filters.
details: setVersionFilter(n,filter,prevConnectionsMode) (1916-1934): adds to recentVersionFilters unless from About; mode 'Version Open' if from About else 'Translation Open'; clearing -> 'Translations'; mirrors onto base panel.

VERIFIED 2026-10-05: the sidebar's version filter lives in the URL as `vside` (panel 1) / `vside{n}`, and only matters for the Translation Open and Version Open views. The rebuild keeps it on the side panel's state and drops it when the view changes.

name: Selected words routed to dictionary lookup
summary: Selecting words in text feeds the Lexicon sidebar.
details: setSelectedWords(n,words) sets next panel's selectedWords when it has no menu (1935-1942); single-panel sets on own panel; words trimmed (ReaderPanel.jsx:339-356).
VERIFIED 2026-10-05: a selection never opens a closed sidebar.

name: Navigate panel to ref with cascade
summary: Moving a panel to a new ref keeps its linked panel in sync.
details: navigatePanel(n,ref,currVersions) sets refs, currentlyVisibleRef, highlightedRefs and cascades to dependent panel (array -> full range highlight; TextAndConnections -> highlight [ref]) (1663-1686).

name: Extended notes view
summary: Books with extended notes can open them from the book page or the sidebar.
details: viewExtendedNotes(n,method,title,vLang,vTitle,family) sets bookRef and single version, then opens 'extended notes' as a menu ('toc') or connectionsMode ('Connections'); backFromExtendedNotes returns to 'book toc' (1687-1706).

name: Show base text / open sheet from panel
summary: Panels can switch to a text or a sheet in place.
details: showBaseText(ref,replaceHistory,currVersions,filter,convert,forceOpenCommentaryPanel) (ReaderPanel.jsx:259-292): Sheet ref routes to openSheet; replaceHistory saves last place first; calls openPanelAt(panelPosition,...,replace=true,...,saveLastPlace=false) carrying current settings.

openSheet(sheetRef) parses 'Sheet id:node' into mode Sheet (293-310); handleSheetClick(sheet,node,highlightedRefsInSheet) opens a sheet in same panel (247-255); handleSheetSegmentClick(source) highlights a node (183-186).
updateTextColumn(refs) handles infinite-scroll ref changes with replaceHistory (311-315); setCurrentlyVisibleRef uses replaceHistory (584-590).

name: Panel menu helpers
summary: Small panel actions for menus: close menus, open a menu, set categories/topic/tab etc.
details: closeMenus(): menuOpen null, or 'navigation' if no refs; clears categories/topic category (357-365). closeSheetMetaData (366-375). openMenu(menu) sets mode Text, resets nav/topic fields (376-386).
setNavigationCategories, setNavigationTopic, setTopic (with topicTestVersion), setCollectionTag, onSetTopicSort, setLinkerEditorBook (push history), updateCollectionName (replace history).
setTab has race-condition workaround for TabView mounting before history push (595-606).

name: Connections mode switching and login gating
summary: Sidebar tools that require an account prompt anonymous users to log in.
details: setConnectionsMode(mode,connectionData) (550-569): 'Add Connection' with one open ref opens compare panel; login-required modes for anonymous -> 'Login' (event 'Tools / Prompt Login'), else event 'Tools / {mode} Click'; 'Resources' clears filter; stores connectionData.
LoginPrompt panel ('Please log in' with login/signup buttons and next) used for 'Login' mode (Misc.jsx:1964-1983).

name: Panel text data loading and current book/category
summary: Each panel loads the text for its visible ref and versions.
details: conditionalSetTextData() clears data and, for Text/TextAndConnections or connectionsMode 'Advanced Tools', calls Sefaria.getTextFromCurrVersions(currentlyVisibleRef,currVersions,translationLanguagePreference,true); re-runs on versions/currentlyVisibleRef/connectionsMode change (66-74,108-112).
currentBook() = data.indexTitle else parsed ref index/book; currentCategory() = 'Sheets' for sheets else index primary_category (619-636).

name: Open library, voices, root, search and user pages
summary: Header/nav actions open the right home or page panel.
details: showLibrary(categories), showVoices(), showRoot() choose by Sefaria.activeModule (2007-2026).
showSearch(query) (2027-2042): labels analytics flow source 'nav_bar' only when not already on search; reuses existing searchState (filtersValid false) or creates new by module type.
searchInCollection(query,collection): sheet search with applied filter [collection], aggType 'collections' (2043-2048).
showSaved, showNotes, showHistory, showTopics, showNotifications, showCalendars, showUserStats, showLinkerEditor(book), showCollections (2049-2075).

openTopic(slug) async Sefaria.getTopic then topics panel with primaryTitle and topicTestVersion; openTopicCategory(slug) (title from topicTocCategoryTitle); openAllTopics(letter); openProfile(slug,tab='sheets') async profileAPI; openCollection(slug,tag); openTranslationsPage(slug) (2081-2108).

name: Single-panel (mobile) behavior differences
summary: Mobile shows one panel at a time; many interactions change rather than add panels.
details: multiPanel gates: segment click (sidebar panel vs in-panel TextAndConnections), citation click, named-entity open, selected-words routing, commentary-ref opening (2 panels vs TextAndConnections), selectVersion dependent-panel cascade.
Mobile links: every in-app link replaces panel via openURL(href,true); in multi-panel, links inside sheet content (.sheetItem) open a NEW panel at end, others replace (ReaderApp.jsx:1215-1244).
Breakpoint check Sefaria.getBreakpoint() === MOBILE gates chatbot, chatbot banner, header variant, Popover placement.
getGuideType returns null on mobile or panelPosition != 0 (ReaderPanel.jsx:492-494).

name: Mobile reader controls as header
summary: On mobile, the in-panel text header replaces the site header while reading.
details: ReaderControls mobile: MenuButton (hamburger -> mobile nav menu) instead of CloseButton; Connections panels in single-panel mode hide reader header (hideHeader) (ReaderPanel.jsx:1399,1455-1460).
Site header hidden on mobile while viewing text (first panel mode Text/TextAndConnections, no menu) unless mobile nav menu open (Header.jsx:223-232).

VERIFIED 2026-10-05 with a phone User-Agent (iPhone, 390px): the site header is hidden while reading; the panel's own header has, left to right, a hamburger (opens the site's mobile navigation menu, which then shows over the text), the title + version, a bookmark (Save) and the display 'A'. Rebuild: menu button in the panel header (CSS swaps it with Close at ≤842px), shared open/closed state (features/shell/mobile-menu.ts), the menu closes on navigation and Escape.

FOUND: the earlier phone parity runs used a desktop User-Agent at 390px, and sefaria.org decides single-panel mode from the User-Agent, so the phone-only rules were never seen. Re-probe phone behaviour with a phone UA (see scripts/parity-search.mjs --mobile).

name: Browser history sync for panel state
summary: The reader pushes or replaces browser history as panel state changes so back/forward and URL sharing work.
details: updateHistoryState(shouldReplace) runs on mount (replace) and after every update unless last update was popstate (ReaderApp.jsx:214,269-313,893-931): resets replaceHistory flag, skips when shouldHistoryUpdate() false, preserves URL #hash.
Replace -> history.replaceState + delayed pageview if URL changed; push -> never pushes identical URL, else pushState + trackPageview; sets <title> and adjusts scrollbar padding.

shouldHistoryUpdate compares per panel: mode, menuOpen, bookRef, last ref, highlightedRefs, filter, refs, currentlyVisibleRef, connectionsMode, connectionData JSON, currVersions, searchQuery, tab, topicSort, collectionName/Tag, linkerEditorBook, searchState (appliedFilters/field/sortType), language, navigationTopicCategory, highlightedNode, aliyotTorah, navigationTopic, navigationCategories, auth show/path (414-483).
Sheet title arrival: re-pushes when sheet title loads and document title is still the placeholder.

name: Back/forward (popstate) restoration
summary: Back and forward restore panel state and scroll position.
details: Popstate (316-354): sets justPopped (skips next history write); rehydrates SearchState objects (history drops class instances); clones panels to avoid aliasing history.state; restores .content scrollTop from state.scrollPosition and triggers scroll.
Labels search analytics flow source 'back_click' when returning into search.
BUG (rebuild, fixed 2026-10-05): going back to an entry created by choosing a verse left the column on the text that had replaced it (the column only restarted for entries without history state).

name: Scroll position persistence in history
summary: Scroll position is saved so returning to a page restores your place.
details: Scroll handler on .content (re-bound after each update) debounces 300ms and writes scrollPosition into current history state via replaceState (270,965-974).

name: Panel state to URL serialization (shell-specific rules)
summary: Multiple panels are encoded into a single URL, with short forms for the common text+sidebar case.
details: Per-menu URL mapping in makeHistoryState (515-671); '&tab=' appended for non-search menus. Search: 'tab' means search type so results tab is 'search_tab'; search-state URL params prefix 't' (text) / 's' (sheet).

Connections: 'sources' = filter joined '+', or connectionsMode if URL-representable (Sheets, Notes, Translations, Translation Open, Version Open, About, AboutSheet, Navigation, WebPages, extended notes, Topics, Torah Readings, manuscripts, Lexicon, SidebarSearch, Guide, LinkerAdmin), else 'all'. ConnectionsList filters get ' ConnectionsList' suffix; WebPagesList -> 'WebPage:{filter}'; SidebarSearch panel borrows previous panel's refs (690-723).

Text URL = normRef(highlighted range if overlaps currentlyVisibleRef else currentlyVisibleRef); aliyot for Torah (672-688). Sheet: panel 0 /sheets/{id}[.{node}], later panels sheet&s={id.node} (752-762).

Merging panels (784-891): panel 0 base URL + ven/vhe + &with= (mobile TextAndConnections) + &lang= + &aliyot= + &debug_mode=linker; short form for Text/Sheet + Connections first two panels; later connections &p{i}=&w{i}=...; other panels &p={url} with = suffixed by index; titles joined ' and '; '?' in titles encoded %3F.
Titles: '{ref} with {mode}' localized via CONNECTION_MODE_STRING_IDS unless 'all'/ConnectionsList.

BUG (VERIFIED 2026-10-04): panel numbers follow the flat panel array, sidebars included, so [Text+Connections, Text] is written as ?with=all&p3=Exodus.1 — and the server stops at the first missing p{i}, so reloading that URL silently drops the third panel. The rebuild numbers logical panels sequentially (p2, w2 for its sidebar), which the old server also reads, and accepts gaps when decoding.
BUG (VERIFIED 2026-10-04): `lang2` means both 'panel 2 language' and 'first sidebar language' (/Genesis.1.1?with=all&p2=Exodus.1&lang2=en is rewritten to …&lang2=en&p3=Exodus.1&lang3=en).

VERIFIED 2026-10-06 on sefaria.org (scripts/probes/multipanel-probe*.mjs, scripts/parity-panels.mjs): the address is rewritten on arrival with the defaults filled in (/Genesis.1 → /Genesis.1?lang=bi&aliyot=0; a sidebar always has lang2). A sidebar takes a number slot: [A+sidebar, B] → ?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en&p3=B&lang3=bi&aliyot3=0; [A, B+sidebar] → …&p2=B&lang2=bi&aliyot2=0&w2=all&lang3=en (the sidebar's language is lang<k+1>); panel 1's aliyot is dropped while its sidebar is open; aliyot is written for Torah books only (titleIsTorah). The old server drops p3 on reload (views.py stops at the first missing p<i>).

OWNER DECISION 2026-10-06: read and write these URLs exactly. BUILT: encodeWorkspace ports makeHistoryState's URL assembly; defaults from the reader's settings; the arrival rewrite uses history.replaceState (same entry and state) after TanStack's deferred pushState. src/lib/workspace/legacy-urls.ts is the recorded corpus, each URL round-trips byte for byte (legacy-urls.test.ts).

name: In-app link routing (openURL)
summary: Clicking internal links navigates within the app without a page reload when possible.
details: openURL(href,replace,overrideContentLang,moduleTarget,signupSource) (1330-1456): confirms unsaved sheet-editor changes first (cancel -> 'handled', no navigation); resolves full URL via Sefaria.util.fullURL.
Non-Sefaria URLs or links targeting another module open in NEW tab; in Voices, ABOUT_SIDEBAR_PAGES open in new Library tab (noopener,noreferrer).
/login,/register -> in-app AuthPage with next; any other path hides auth.

Routes handled in-app: /, /texts[/cats], /history, /saved, /texts/notes, /collections, /collections/{slug} (not /settings,/new) with tag, /my/profile, /profile/{slug}, /notifications, /calendars, /torahtracker, /linker-editor?book=, /sheets/{id}, /topics, /topics/category/{slug}, /topics/all/{letter}, /topics/{slug}, /translations/{slug}, any ref path (%3F->?; ven/vhe from query; showHighlight if ranged); else returns false (normal browser navigation).
lastOpenURLNavigatedInApp() distinguishes real in-app navigation from new-tab/cancel (1457-1465).

name: External bootstrap-url event
summary: An external script can ask the app to navigate to a ref or URL.
details: bootstrapUrl(href,{replaceHistory}) (1246-1258,1272-1303): validates URL; accepts only same host or *sefaria.org; refs go through handleNavigationClick(humanRef) respecting replaceHistory, other paths via openURL.
Guarded by unsaved-editor confirm (1288-1292). No dispatcher in repo (see findings).

name: In-app link interception and modifier keys
summary: Plain clicks stay in the app; modified clicks and right-click open normally, even across module subdomains.
details: handleInAppLinkClick (1182-1245) ignores default-prevented events, legacy Sheet Builder pages (typeof sjs !== 'undefined'), non-<a> targets, non-_self targets, links without href; reads data-target-module and data-signup-source via closest.

Capture-phase document handler handleInAppClickWithModifiers lets ctrl/cmd/shift/alt-clicks fall through to browser; stops propagation, rewrites data-target-module hrefs to full module URL, reports modified search-result click for analytics (229,1152-1172).
Right-click (contextmenu) on a[data-target-module] rewrites href to correct subdomain so 'open in new tab' works (234,1305-1328).

name: Per-panel search state management
summary: Search filters and sort are tracked per panel and survive history navigation.
details: updateQuery (invalidates filters), updateSearchState, updateAvailableFilters (registers available, registry, orphan filters, aggregationsToUpdate; filtersValid true), resetSearchFilters (unselect all nodes, clear applied filters/aggTypes/registry), updateSearchFilter (toggle node, recompute applied), updateSearchOptionField, updateSearchOptionSort (1469-1541).
unsetTextHighlight(n) clears search-term highlighting (1466-1468).

name: Escape closes panel
summary: Pressing Escape inside a panel closes it.
details: handleKeyPress keyCode 27 -> closePanel (ReaderPanel.jsx:646-650); applies to ANY panel including the text panel.
Rebuild: Escape in a panel closes it unless a menu, dialog or input already used the key.

name: Reader panel context
summary: Per-panel display state is shared with child components through a context.
details: ReaderPanelContext (display name 'ContentLanguageContext'; default {language:'english'}) (context.js:16-19). Provides: language override, isMenuOpen, setIsMenuOpen, setOption, textsData, layout, panelMode, aliyotShowStatus, vowelsAndCantillationState, punctuationState, width, panelPosition (ReaderPanel.jsx:736-749).

name: Shared React hooks
summary: Utility hooks for language resolution, debouncing and incremental loading.
details: useContentLang(defaultToInterfaceOnBilingual,override) resolves language from context and text data (primaryLang/translationLang); ambiguous -> interface language.

useDebounce; useScrollToLoad (skip/limit pagination within 600px of bottom); usePaginatedDisplay (client-side paging on scroll, default 800px margin); useIncrementalLoad/usePaginatedLoad (chunked fetching, cancellation by identity element).

name: In-panel text header (ReaderControls)
summary: Each text panel has a header with title, subtitle, save and display settings.
details: Shown unless panel is TextAndConnections, Sheet, has menu open, or hideNavHeader set (ReaderPanel.jsx:1172-1177); Sheet header comes from Sheet itself.

Title: Sheet -> sheet icon + title ('Loading...' until loaded; getSheetTitle), dir auto; Text -> {indexTitle}{section} / Hebrew equivalent via ContentText (bilingual defaults to interface language). Link href /sheets/{id} or /{Book} with data-target-module (Voices for sheets).
Clicking title opens connections panel for currentRef (event 'Reader / Open Connections Panel from Header'); sheets call onSheetTitleClick(0) (1308-1318,1423-1453).

Left buttons: CloseButton (multi-panel) or MenuButton (mobile); hidden placeholder SaveButton for symmetry (1455-1460). CategoryColorLine above (except in connections header), coloured by current category (1505).
connectionsMode passed as 'Connection Text' when a filter exists and mode is 'Connections' (1207).

VERIFIED: the text header has a Save button (aria-label 'Save "Genesis 1"', a bookmark) before the display-options 'A'. Signed out it opens the 'Want to return to this text?' sign-up modal (Save texts / Take notes / View your reading history / Build & share source sheets; Sign Up, Already have an account? Sign in). Rebuild: built (it was missing); the modal is the existing 'save' kind.

VERIFIED geometry (1280px, no sidebar): the text header's controls sit inside the text's own 700px column (Close at x=290, title centred at 640, Save at 932, display 'A' at 969), not at the panel's edges; title 18px Cardo, version line 15px italic #6f6f6f; the bar is 60px under a 4px category colour line. Rebuilt (the bar was full-width with a 13px subtitle).

Rebuild guard (found when the 15px version line made two subtitle lines taller than the bar): the text header is ALWAYS 60px — title on a 21px line, version/attribution lines 17px each — so choosing a version (which adds a line) never moves the text below it (e2e/about.spec.ts).
2026-10-07: the Save button now works (USL-011).

name: Unsaved sheet-editor change protection
summary: Leaving the editor with unsaved changes prompts for confirmation (in-app navigation only).
details: shouldAlertBeforeCloseEditor(): panel 0 is Sheet, editorSaveState !== 'saved', shouldUseEditor(sheetId) (ReaderApp.jsx:1947-1954).
window.confirm('You have unsaved changes that may be lost. Continue?') guards openURL, bootstrapUrl, closePanel(0) (1141-1151,1288-1292,1337-1341,1958-1962).
No browser-level beforeunload, so reload/tab close loses changes.

name: Custom copy formatting for selected text
summary: Copied text is cleaned of numbers and UI chrome so it pastes nicely.
details: handleCopyEvent (ReaderApp.jsx:2239-2336): ignored from INPUT, TEXTAREA, LC-CHATBOT. Clones selection into container.
Non-continuous panels: each .contentSpan becomes <div dir=rtl|ltr> (direction detected). Hebrew panels container dir=rtl. .poetry wrappers collapsed (fixes Google Docs paste in Chrome).

Continuous panels:
removed; .segment,.rangeSpan,.segmentText,.contentSpan collapsed.

Removed: .segmentNumber, .linkCount, .clearFix, .footnote-marker, hidden footnotes (not display:inline); open footnotes prefixed ' *'. a.namedEntityLink and a.refLink stripped to plain text; all spans except .rangeSpan collapsed.
Sets text/plain (via htmlToText) and text/html on clipboard and prevents default.

VERIFIED 2026-10-05 (Genesis 1:1-3, bilingual, copy event listener on the live page): text/html is `

HEBREW
ENGLISH

…
` — segment and rangeSpan wrappers survive, numbers, dots, footnote markers ('a', 'b') and links are gone, the drop-cap survives; text/plain is one line per version, each ending in a newline (trailing spaces kept); the event is default-prevented; no citation is appended.

Rebuild: cleaned in src/lib/reader/copy.ts — one <div dir> per version, no segment wrappers (simpler markup, same text), plain text trimmed; continuous layout is running text; open footnotes are copied after ' *'. Hooks: TextColumn onCopy.

name: Reader text column renders sections of text
summary: The reader shows a scrolling column of text sections, each made of numbered segments, in the main panel and side panels.
details: Chain: ReaderPanel -> TextColumn -> TextRange (one per section ref) -> TextSegment -> VersionContent/ContentSpan.
ReaderPanel builds TextColumn only for modes Text and TextAndConnections; provides ReaderPanelContext (language, layout, panelMode, textsData, aliyot/vowels/punctuation, width, panelPosition).
VersionContent/ContentSpan render raw HTML via dangerouslySetInnerHTML as 'contentSpan he|en primary|translation'.
ContentText is a generic bilingual renderer filtered by content language (useContentLang); used for titles, numbers, headers.
Other TextRange consumers: TextList (connections), VersionsTextList, MyNotesPanel, GuideBox.

name: TextRange load, redirect and prefetch
summary: When a section loads, the reader normalizes odd refs and prefetches neighbors and links.
details: onTextLoad (basetext): (a) sref !== data.ref -> replace with normalized ref (no new history); (b) spanning -> replace with spanningRefs; (c) super-section -> redirect to firstAvailableSectionRef.
Prefetch: links for each section (Sefaria.related, plus relatedPrivate if logged in; ranged refs trimmed), next/prev text with same versions, getIndexDetails.
If filterRef set, matching [data-ref] element in connections panel is scrolled into view.
shouldComponentUpdate re-renders on sref, filter, highlight, versions, translation pref, language, layouts, aliyot, vowels, biLayout, fontSize, punctuation, layoutWidth, data.
DEAD: prefetchMultiple (20 for dictionaries) passed but never read; showActionLinks renders undefined actionLinks (would throw).

name: Dead actionLinks and prefetchMultiple props
summary: Two reader options exist in code that do nothing or would break.
details: DEAD: showActionLinks renders undefined actionLinks variable (TextRange.jsx:393); CSS .textRange .actionLinks legacy.
DEAD: prefetchMultiple passed (20 for dictionaries) but never read.

name: Fetch text via v3 texts API with versions
summary: Text for a section is loaded with the user's chosen source and translation versions, with gaps filled in.
details: getTextFromCurrVersions -> _getPrimaryAndTranslationText -> _getVersionObjects -> getTextsFromAPIV3 (fill_in_missing_segments=1, return_format=wrap_all_entities) -> _adaptApiResponse.
makeUrlForAPIV3Text: /api/v3/texts/<normRef>?version=<lang|vtitle>... ; version params sorted; response cached in _textsStore keyed by URL (_cachedApiPromise).
withContext on a segment ref: refetches the section ref and replaces text/he/alts with section-level arrays; other metadata (ref, sections, highlight) stays segment-level.
Result saved into legacy text cache via _saveText.
BUG: _makeV3VersionsUrlCacheKey calls versions.map(...) and discards the result, so the SSR-seeded cache key may not match the client request URL and the first client fetch can miss the cache.

name: Client picks source and translation versions
summary: The reader decides which Hebrew/primary and translation versions to show using the user's selection, per-corpus preference and language preference.
details: _getVersionObjects loads all versions (/api/texts/versions/<ref>). Primary = highest-priority isPrimary version matching currVersions.he, else {languageFamilyName:'primary'}.

Translation: if currVersions.en.versionTitle set it must match a non-source version; else fallback order: (1) per-corpus preference getVersionPref(ref).en, (2) translationLanguagePreference bucket (highest-priority non-source), (3) {languageFamilyName:'translation'} (server picks highest priority).
_findInVersions picks highest priority among matches.
setVersionPreference records only en (translation) prefs per corpus and saves them to the profile.
Per-corpus preference override applies only to panels 2+ on SSR (override_version_with_preference).

name: Adapt v3 API response to legacy text shape
summary: The newer text API response is converted into the older field layout the reader components expect.
details: getPrimaryAndTranslationFromVersions: single version -> translation={text:[]}; if versions[0].isPrimary && !versions[1].isSource order is [primary, translation] else swapped.
Translation -> text, versionTitle, translationDirection, translationLang, versionStatus. Primary -> he, heVersionTitle, primaryDirection, primaryLang, heVersionStatus.
sources/heSources mark merged versions; ReaderControls hides version title when data.sources is set; BookPage sets currentVersion.merged = !!sources.
BUG: heSources condition looks inverted: sources set when translation sources differ but heSources set when primary sources are all the same (sefaria.js:773-778).

name: Legacy text cache with per-segment entries
summary: Fetched text is cached per segment and section so neighbors, context and spanning refs load instantly.
details: _saveText stores by _textKey (ref + ven/vhe + transLangPref + FALLBACK + |CONTEXT); section data split into per-segment entries (_splitTextSection) each with nextSegment/prevSegment and a buildable 'Add Context' placeholder.
Context saves a section-level copy; spanning refs prime every spanning section via getText.
Super-sections (textDepth = sections+2, e.g. a commentary chapter): _splitTextSection computes next/prev per child section so empty sub-sections are skipped.
index_offsets_by_depth (_get_offsets) lets numbering start at an offset; used in segment numbering and splitting.
Sefaria.ref()/getRefFromCache is a cache-only synchronous lookup; infinite scroll depends on it so only prefetched neighbors chain. getRef is the promise form.
_splitTextSection delimiter is ' ' when data.ref === data.book (depth-1 at root).

name: Server-rendered panel text seeded into client
summary: The first text panel arrives already rendered from the server and is then refreshed by the client.
details: Sefaria.unpackDataFromProps puts each SSR panel's text into _textsStore and _saveText (context=1), saves available_versions, indexDetails and sheet data.

make_panel_dict: book-level refs -> book TOC menu; else ref replaced by first_available_section_ref(), spanning refs split; server prefetches section via TextRequestAdapter(return_format='wrap_all_entities'); maps to he/text.
updateFromAPI: True is set so the client refetches.
Segment-level or range refs -> highlightedRefs = each segment.
Meta description uses first section's segment text truncated to 160 chars (_reduce_ranged_ref_text_to_first_section).

name: Build numbered segments from text data
summary: Raw text arrays are turned into numbered, addressable segments with highlight and alt-structure markers.
details: makeSegments pads text and he to equal length; numbers start at sections[-1] for a segment ref without context, else 1 + offset.
Ref per segment: sectionRef + (textDepth==1 ? ' ' : ':') + number.
highlight true when ref is segment-level and number within [sections[-1], toSections[-1]]; alt = data.alts[i] (used for parashah/aliyah headers).
Spanning data: iterates sections; highlight covers first section from start, middle fully, last to its end.
stripImagesFromSegments is used by sheet editors only.

name: Section title strings (named vs numbered)
summary: Each section gets a title such as 'Chapter 4' or '2a' in English and Hebrew.
details: Sefaria.sectionString returns {en:{named,numbered},he:{named,numbered}}.
English named prepends sectionNames[0] when depth > 1; complex texts prepend the named node path ('Introduction, Chapter 2').
Hebrew uses heSectionRef minus heIndexTitle; Hebrew section names are commented out.

name: Section title in text column
summary: Each section shows a title like 'Chapter 4' or '2a' above its text.
details: Short numbered title (useShortString) for primary_category in {Tanakh, Mishnah, Talmud, Tanaitic, Commentary}; named title for others ('Chapter 4', 'Introduction, Chapter 2').
Rendered .title > .titleBox with bilingual title defaulting to interface language; optional titleButtons; non-basetext title = full ref/heRef.
Title CSS: centered, 1.1em, light, letter-spaced with 4px underline.

name: Reader header title and version label
summary: The reader header shows the book and current section with the active translation's name.
details: Title = indexTitle + section string from data.ref (Hebrew from heRef); bilingual defaults to interface language; click opens connections for current ref unless sidebar open.
Version title shown when language is english/bilingual and version not merged; prefers shortVersionTitle / shortVersionTitleInHebrew.
CategoryColorLine by category ('Sheets' for sheets).
Header/menu data from conditionalSetTextData loading currentlyVisibleRef with context; refreshes on version, visible ref or connections-mode change.

VERIFIED 2026-10-05: title = indexTitle + section part, in the language of the version on screen (ReaderPanelContext via useContentLang): Hebrew mode → source language; English mode → the TRANSLATION's language family; bilingual, or a family other than english/hebrew → the interface language. So /Zohar,_Bereshit.1?lang=en has a Hebrew title ('ספר הזהר, בראשית א׳') because its translation is Hebrew; Genesis lang=he → 'בראשית א׳'.

VERIFIED 2026-10-05: the version line shows only in English and bilingual modes (never Hebrew-only) and is the translation's shortVersionTitle, else its versionTitle. Genesis he: no version line; Berakhot he: only the attribution.
The header is hidden entirely on phones when the sidebar is open (mode TextAndConnections; ReaderPanel.hideReaderControls).

name: Client ref parsing and helpers for text addressing
summary: The client parses, normalizes and compares refs, including dafs, ranges and dictionary entries.
details: parseRef uses booksDict; handles Sheet, virtualBooks (dictionary/lexicon titles with trailing number), requires a space after book title ('Jobs' != 'Job'), ranges with '-', Talmud \d+[ab].
Helpers: humanRef, normRef, makeRef, normRefList, joinRefList (Hebrew via cache), refContains (daf-aware), splitRangingRef (uses cached text), zoomOutRef, sectionRef.
BUG: client parseRef accepts only \d+[ab]? addresses; Folio c/d (intToFolio) fails with 'Bad section string'; refContains converts only a/b dafs.
DEAD: wrapRefLinks/makeRefRe (client-side citation wrapping into span.refLink) not used by the current reader; refs arrive pre-wrapped from server.

name: Section label by address type for TOC
summary: Table-of-contents section labels follow each text's addressing scheme (daf, year, folio, number).
details: getSectionStringByAddressType: Talmud -> intToDaf/encodeHebrewDaf; Year -> i+1241 with Hebrew numeral and gershayim; Folio -> intToFolio/encodeHebrewFolio; else integer+1 / Hebrew numeral.
Used by BookPage TOC only; reader segment numbers stay integers/Hebrew numerals regardless of address type.

name: v3 texts API parameters and warnings
summary: The text API accepts version selectors and return formats and reports missing versions.
details: /api/v3/texts/<tref>: version= repeatable (lang|vtitle; lang may be primary/source/translation/language family/empty; vtitle may be 'all'), fill_in_missing_segments, return_format in default|wrap_all_entities|text_only|strip_only_footnotes, debug_mode.
404 for empty non-virtual refs; virtual nodes (dictionaries) allowed even when 'empty'.
warnings: APINoVersion 101, APINoLanguageVersion 102, APINoSourceText 103, APINoTranslationText 104.
BUG/GAP: client ignores API warnings; no 'missing translation' notice in the reader.

name: TextRequestAdapter version resolution and payload
summary: The server resolves requested versions, merges gaps and returns text plus ref, index and node metadata.
details: get_versions_for_query applies default_child_ref() first (default nodes of complex texts).
_append_required_versions: exact vtitle match is strict, else max-priority (resolve_default_version); duplicates suppressed; unmatched to 'missings'.

_append_version builds a TextChunk with merge_versions limited to the same languageFamilyName; attaches sources only if merged from >1 version; adds firstSectionRef for book-level refs; each version carries all Version fields (direction, isPrimary, isSource, formatAsPoetry, shortVersionTitle, status, license, priority, etc.).

Ref data: ref, heRef, sections/toSections (normalized strings), sectionRef, heSectionRef, firstAvailableSectionRef, isSpanning/spanningRefs, next/prev, title, book, primary_category, type (=primary_category).

Index/node data: indexTitle, categories, isComplex, isDependant, order, collectiveTitle, alts, lengths, textDepth, sectionNames, addressTypes, titleVariants, index_offsets_by_depth (skipped for virtual nodes).
Top-level available_langs and available_versions (used by ReaderControls for shortVersionTitle).
Debug_mode=linker adds raw LinkerOutput records.

name: Return formats and text cleaning
summary: The API can return text with inline links, plain text, or footnote-stripped text.
details: wrap_all_entities applies MarkedUpTextChunk spans per segment (citations, named entities, categories).
text_only strips itags and HTML and collapses whitespace; strip_only_footnotes strips itags and collapses whitespace.

AbstractTextRecord.strip_itags removes footnotes, other itags and fn-markers; remove_html turns
into a space.

name: Merge versions segment by segment
summary: When the chosen version has gaps, missing segments are filled from the next-best version of the same language.
details: merge_texts fills gaps segment by segment from highest-priority non-empty version; returns parallel sources arrays (one versionTitle per segment).
Merging limited to same languageFamilyName; SSR passes fill_in_missing_segments default True.

name: Allowed inline HTML in stored text
summary: Stored texts may contain a fixed set of formatting tags, footnotes, images, and overlay markers.
details: Tags: i b br u strong em big small img sup sub span a.
Attributes: sup[class]; span[class,dir]; i[data-overlay,data-value,data-commentator,data-order,class,data-label,dir]; img[src,alt]; a[dir,class,href,data-ref,data-ven,data-vhe,data-scroll-link].
i tags serve three uses: footnotes, commentary placement (itags) and structure overlays such as page transitions.
No mam-* (Miqra al pi ha-Masorah) or ktiv/kri classes exist in CSS; big -> 1.2em, other tags browser default.

name: Inline citation links in text (refLink)
summary: Citations inside a text are clickable links that open the cited source.
details: Server wraps citations via CitationMUTCSpan -> <a class='refLink' href data-ref data-range>; uses LLM-disambiguated ref when present; book-level refs left unlinked in non-debug mode.
Manually wrapped refs also supported (hasManuallyWrappedRefs). Client never wraps citations itself in the reader.
refLink style: 0.8em bold, letter-spaced, #333, underline on hover.

data-scroll-link='true' into same book -> navigatePanel scrolls same panel; otherwise onCitationClick honoring data-ven/data-vhe. Multipanel opens new panel after current (closing a connections panel); mobile replaces base text.

name: Inline named-entity (topic) links in text
summary: People and concepts named in the text are underlined links that open the topic/lexicon sidebar.
details: NamedEntityMUTCSpan -> <a class='namedEntityLink' href='/topics/slug' data-slug>. Click selects link text and opens Lexicon/topic sidebar (connectionsMode 'Lexicon', selectedNamedEntity slug); topic fetched with getTopic(slug,{annotated:false}).
Hover underline only with .showNamedEntityLinks.
URL params namedEntity, namedEntityText. Clicking another segment closes the named entity (closeNamedEntityInConnectionPanel).
Named entities on Jerusalem Talmud show a hard-coded data-source sentence ('...by Sefaria') instead of Michael Sperling attribution (LexiconBox.jsx:114-119).

VERIFIED 2026-10-05 (Berakhot 2a, English): clicking 'Rabbi Eliezer' selects the verse and the address becomes /Berakhot.2a.1?namedEntity=rabbi-eliezer-b-hyrcanus&namedEntityText=Rabbi Eliezer&with=Lexicon; the sidebar shows 'Rabbi Eliezer b. Hyrcanus' (link to /topics/<slug>, new tab) + 'Tannaim - Third Generation' + 'c.80 – c.110 CE' + the markdown description. Request: GET /api/v2/topics/<slug>?annotate_time_period=1&ref_link_type_filters=about|popular-writing-of&with_html=0&with_links=0&annotate_links=0&with_refs=0&group_related=0&with_indexes=0.

An ambiguous name's slug ends in '-(ambiguous)' (e.g. /topics/רג-(ambiguous)); the response then carries `possibilities` (Rabban Gamliel → three people) and the sidebar says '"Rabban Gamliel" could refer to one of the following:' / 'ייתכן ש-"…" מתייחס לאחד מהבאים:' above each. No description: "No description known for '<title>'" / "לא קיים מידע עבור '<title>'".

Rebuild: links in the text carry the library's absolute /topics URL (a modified click or a new tab works), a plain click opens the sidebar; choosing another verse ends the card (back to Resources). Params namedEntity, namedEntityText (+N per panel) in the workspace URL.

name: Inline category links in text
summary: Mentions of a category name in the text can link to that category in the library.
details: CategoryMUTCSpan -> <a class='categoryLink' href='/texts/path' data-category-path>.

name: Entity span safety rules
summary: Stale or invalid link annotations are skipped so edited text never shows broken links.
details: apply_spans_to_text inserts spans from end of string backwards; skips deleted spans (unless debug); clamps out-of-range spans.
Skips a span if its text no longer matches the segment (stale after an edit).

name: Footnotes toggle inline
summary: Footnote markers in the text expand and collapse the footnote text in place.
details: Click on sup (or inside it) toggles the next i.footnote and re-places segment numbers.
CSS: sup 0.6em Hebrew sans; sup.footnote-marker and sup.endFootnote link blue with hover underline; sup::before enlarges click target; i.footnote hidden by default, 0.8em, dark grey, not italic.
Footnote markers hidden in print; copy handler removes closed footnotes and prefixes open ones with ' *'.

BUG-COMPAT (VERIFIED 2026-10-05, Ramban on Genesis 1:1:3 English): the stored HTML is mis-nested — '(See Rashi, ibid.) It was thus…' inside a footnote — and the browser's HTML5 parser repairs it so the whole footnote stays hidden; a plain tag parser ends the footnote at the first and leaks its tail ') It was thus … created.' into the text. The rebuild now repairs mis-nested inline markup with parse5 before extracting footnotes (src/lib/html/repair.ts).

name: Inline images in text
summary: Texts can contain whole-segment images with captions and inline images in running text.
details: Full-segment image (segment is exactly one , isFullSegmentImage regex /^\s*]*>\s*$/i): VersionImageSpan renders .image-in-text > img + p.image-in-text-title (alt as caption); onLoad re-places segment numbers.
In bilingual mode, if both sides are images the primary image is suppressed (translation preferred).
CSS: centered flex, responsive widths, aspect-ratio rules. Inline images stay in HTML with .segment img {max-width:100%}.

name: Inline commentary markers (itags)
summary: When a commentary is selected in connections, numbered markers appear in the base text where that commentator comments.
details: formatItag only when a connections filter is active: replaces <i data-commentator='<filter[0]>'> with <sup class='itag'> showing data-label or data-order (Hebrew numeral in he). Quotes in commentator name escaped.
Without a filter the <i> markers stay empty and invisible. CSS .segment sup.itag. Hidden in print.
Link-count dots reflect only the filtered commentator.

name: Page-transition overlay markers
summary: Page and column breaks of printed editions appear as small markers inside the text.
details: i[data-overlay='Vilna Pages'] and i[data-overlay='Venice Columns'] render content: attr(data-value) as small grey sans marker (Talmud page/column transitions).

PARITY NOTE 2026-10-05: Vilna/Venice page markers are an empty <i data-overlay data-value> on the live site (shown by CSS, absent from innerText) and a text node in the rebuild; visually equivalent (small grey marker at the line start/end).

name: Search-term highlighting in text
summary: When arriving from search, the matched words are highlighted inside the opened segment.
details: addHighlights wraps each word of each textHighlights term in a regex tolerant of interleaved HTML tags, then wraps matches in span.queryTextHighlight.
Applied in basetext only to highlighted segments; cleared (unsetTextHighlight) when highlight moves.

name: Linker debug mode spans
summary: In debug mode, auto-detected citations are color-coded by status for moderators.
details: ?debug_mode=linker adds debug_mode=linker to v3 requests; spans classed 'mutc spanDeleted|spanFailed|spanDisambiguated|spanAmbiguous|spanSucceeded'; linker_output stored in Sefaria._linkerOutputMap keyed ref|lang|start-end.
Click a span: moderator with citation span opens LinkerAdmin sidebar (with=LinkerAdmin&debug_mode=linker); others get an alert with debug info and linker_test.py test string.
Only for LinkerOutput class path; classes styled at s2.css:7377-7407.

name: Language display: Source / Translation / Bilingual
summary: Readers choose to see the source text, a translation, or both together.
details: language values: hebrew (=Source/primary), english (=Translation), bilingual. Persisted as cookie and sets contentLang cookie + app-wide default for new panels.
Panel language inferred from URL versions: only vhe -> hebrew, only ven -> english, both -> bilingual.
URL lang=he|en|bi; openURL with lang param overrides default content language.
Initial language from middleware contentLang: ?lang -> cookie contentLang -> default (hebrew interface -> hebrew, else bilingual); non-TORAH_SPECIFIC sites forced english.
Side/connections panels hide the bilingual option.
Content-language override: menus/connections panels mono-lingual (bilingual becomes english in English UI; always hebrew in Hebrew UI); topics/calendars/collections bilingual (English UI) or hebrew.
Rebuild: the third option reads 'Source with Translation' (not 'Both').

name: Language toggle visibility rule in display menu
summary: The Source/Translation buttons only appear under certain conditions.
details: Visible only if TORAH_SPECIFIC or if the text lacks he or text (ReaderDisplayOptionsMenu.jsx:27-33). Looks inverted but is current behavior; TORAH_SPECIFIC true on sefaria.org so always shown there.
Bilingual option hidden in side panels.

name: Layout: segmented vs continuous
summary: Readers can show text as one verse/segment per line or as a flowing paragraph.
details: Settings layoutDefault / layoutTanakh / layoutTalmud (segmented|continuous); chosen by getLayoutCategory(): primary_category Tanakh -> layoutTanakh, Talmud -> layoutTalmud, else layoutDefault.
Defaults: layoutDefault segmented, layoutTalmud continuous, layoutTanakh segmented.
Connections panel always rendered segmented.

Continuous CSS: .continuous .segment {display:inline} with small vertical padding (less in English to keep named-entity underlines visible); .clearFix and
hidden.
Segmented CSS: block with 26px bottom margin.
Menu labels: 'show text as a paragraph', 'segmented'.

name: Bilingual layout: stacked / side by side
summary: In bilingual mode the translation can sit under the source or beside it, with either side on the left.
details: biLayout stacked | heLeft | heRight (default stacked); used only when language is bilingual and panel width > 500, else forced stacked.
Layout menu state mono -> [continuous, segmented]; bi-rtl -> [stacked, heRight]; bi-ltr -> [stacked, heLeft]; mixed (directions differ, or a sheet) -> [stacked, heLeft, heRight] (constants.js).
Icons /static/icons/{state}-{option}.svg; mixed icons encode direction order (mixed-beside-rtlltr.svg etc.). Labels: 'stacked', 'RTL right of LTR', 'RTL left of LTR'.
Layout buttons hidden when width <= 600 and bilingual, or on a sheet not bilingual.
Stacked CSS: 14px gap between segments; translation margin 10/20px and dark grey. heLeft/heRight: each side 50% width with floats keyed by primary/translation.
Link dots hidden (visibility) in heLeft/heRight; segment number centered between columns (left 50%).

name: Auto side-by-side direction correction
summary: When source and translation read in the same direction, side-by-side layout flips to the sensible order automatically.
details: In side-by-side mode, when primary and translation share a direction (e.g. Hebrew translation of Aramaic, Arabic), biLayout is set to heRight (rtl) or heLeft (ltr).

name: Font size controls
summary: Readers can make text smaller or larger.
details: fontSize numeric percent, default 62.5; smaller/larger divide or multiply by 1.15; applied as inline style.fontSize on .readerContent.
Basetext box font-size 2.2em x panel fontSize%.
Persisted as cookie.

name: Vowels (nikkud) toggle
summary: Readers can hide Hebrew vowel points.
details: vowels all | partial (no cantillation) | none; default all.
Toggle shown only if first sample of he (when showing primary) or text (when showing translation) matches [\u05b0-\u05c3\u05c7].
Toggle off -> none; on -> partial (not all) so cantillation must be re-enabled separately.
Applied to both he and en strings so RTL translations with vowels are stripped too.

name: Cantillation (te'amim) toggle
summary: Readers can hide Hebrew cantillation marks while keeping vowels.
details: Toggle shown if sample matches [\u0591-\u05af]; disabled while vowels are off; toggles partial <-> all.
nre (cantillation only) = [\u0591-\u05af\u05bd\u05bf\u05c0\u05c4\u05c5\u200d]; cnre (cantillation+nikkud) = [\u0591-\u05bd\u05bf-\u05c5\u05c7\u200d].
Active when language != english and vowels != all: partial -> nre, none -> cnre.

BUG: stripping is gated on the first segment: if segment 0's Hebrew has no vowels (e.g. empty), stripping is off for the whole section; regexes carry /g and are used with .test(), so lastIndex is stateful.

name: Color theme (light / sepia / dark)
summary: Reader panels are fully styled for light, sepia and dark themes.
details: color setting stored as cookie (default light) and applied as panel class; extensive CSS (.readerPanel.sepia/.dark; highlight sepia #E3E3E1, dark #444).
DEAD (UI): ReaderDisplayOptionsMenu has no control for color; only a pre-existing cookie can turn it on.

name: Reader panel CSS state classes
summary: The panel carries classes that drive language, layout, direction and narrow-width styling.
details: Classes: readerPanel serif narrowColumn(width<730) <language> <layout> <color>; plus rtl/ltr of shown text when not bilingual or no translation.
Interface direction overrides: Hebrew interface + ltr panel -> textRange ltr; English interface + rtl panel -> textRange rtl.
Language hiding rules: .readerPanel.english .contentSpan.primary, .readerPanel.hebrew .contentSpan.translation, etc.

VERIFIED on a phone UA: `.singlePanel .basetext .text { padding: 0 34px }` — the text runs from x=34 to x=356 at 390px (322px wide), Hebrew right-aligned inside justified paragraphs; with a desktop UA at the same width it is x=56 (narrowColumn). Rebuild: 34px under (max-width: 842px) and (pointer: coarse).

name: Display options menu
summary: One menu groups language, layout, aliyot, font size, vowels, cantillation and punctuation controls.
details: Sections: Source/Translation radios, Layout radio group, Aliyot toggle, Font size -/+, Vowels, Cantillation, Punctuation.
Side panels (non-Text, non-Sheet) show only language buttons.
a11y: focus trap, arrow keys reserved for radios, Escape closes.
All settings persisted as cookies on every change via setOption (ReaderPanel.jsx:530-549).

VERIFIED 2026-10-05 (sefaria.org desktop, Genesis, bilingual): the display menu is a 258px white card (radius 5, 14px Roboto): 1) THREE full-width rows, 235×35 radius 6, 'Source' / 'Translation' / 'Source with Translation', the chosen one #18345d with white text, a 20px radio circle at the end (aria group 'Source-translation toggle'); 2) rule; 3) 'Layout' + three 36×32 icon tiles (aria 'Show Source & Translation Stacked', 'Show RTL Text Left of LTR Text', 'Show RTL Text Right of LTR Text'), the chosen one dark; 4) 'Aliyot' switch (46×24 pill); 5) rule; 6) ⊖ 'Font Size' ⊕ (24px circled icons, no percentage); 7) rule; 8) 'Vowels' and 'Cantillation' switches. Order: language, layout, aliyot, font size, vowels, cantillation. Hovering the trigger shows the tooltip 'Text display options'. Rebuilt to this (it was a segmented Source/Translation/Both with headings and a Stepper; the Stepper component is removed).
Not yet: the hover tooltip on the trigger; the Hebrew-interface strings were not re-verified.

name: Initial settings defaults from cookies
summary: New visitors and returning readers get sensible default reading settings.
details: SSR defaults (base_props): layoutDefault segmented, layoutTalmud continuous, layoutTanakh segmented, aliyotTorah aliyotOff, vowels all, punctuationTalmud punctuationOn, biLayout stacked, color light, fontSize 62.5.
Client fallback defaults at ReaderApp.jsx:976-993.

name: Primary vs translation visibility per segment
summary: Each segment shows the source, the translation, or both depending on language setting and what exists.
details: Primary shown if language != english OR there is no translation; translation shown if language != hebrew OR there is no primary (e.g. VersionsTextList 'Translation Open').
Each side carries its own direction from the version.
Segments with neither side are not rendered.
No translation -> primary shown even in 'english' mode (heOnly class); no 'missing translation' notice.

name: RTL translations rendered with Hebrew styling
summary: Right-to-left translations (Arabic, Persian, Yiddish, Judeo-Arabic) and LTR sources display correctly.
details: VersionContent maps direction -> language class: rtl -> he, ltr -> en; so RTL translation is 'contentSpan he translation' and LTR primary 'contentSpan en primary'. CSS keys floats/stacking on .primary/.translation not language.
.he.translation uses Hebrew sans font at 100% size; in stacked mode black vs dark-grey English translation.
ISOMap with each language's defaultDirection (sefaria.js:891-910). _sortVersionsIntoBuckets derives actual language from a [xx] suffix on versionTitle.
Direction classes: heOnly/enOnly when no translation by primary direction; in Connections panelMode class follows shown side.
.he gets unicode-bidi: plaintext; font switching via --is-hebrew CSS variable trick.

name: Segment numbers
summary: Each verse/segment shows its number in the margin, in Hebrew numerals for Hebrew.
details: segmentNumber > segmentNumberInner: en integer, he encodeHebrewNumeral; in bilingual uses interface language.
Client segment numbers are always integers/Hebrew numerals regardless of address type.
Shown only for basetext; hidden for Guide for the Perplexed, Liturgy and Reference categories.
Positions: ltr panel number left -48; rtl/bilingual number right -46; singlePanel +/-30px; heLeft/heRight centered between columns.
In English/bilingual panels a heOnly segment shows English numeral; in a hebrew panel an enOnly segment shows Hebrew numeral.
CORRECTION (VERIFIED 2026-10-05, Psalms 119 in Hebrew): Hebrew segment numbers are plain letters — א … יט טו טז … קיט — with NO geresh/gershayim ('טו', not 'ט״ו'). The rebuild had added punctuation.

CORRECTION (VERIFIED, Zohar Bereshit 1 in English mode): the 'English' slot of Zohar is a Hebrew translation; its segments are numbered in HEBREW (א, ב) there. The rule 'a Hebrew-only segment in an English/bilingual panel shows an English numeral' holds for a Hebrew PRIMARY shown alone (Arukh HaShulchan 1:13 in English mode: '13' with the Hebrew text) but not for a Hebrew TRANSLATION. The number's language follows the slot and its direction.

name: Segment number and dot positioning in continuous mode
summary: In continuous layout, numbers and link dots are positioned at their segment's start line without overlapping.
details: placeSegmentNumbers (jQuery): sets top of each .segmentNumber and .linkCount from parent segment's top.
Collision fix: two numbers at same top are shifted apart by widths toward reading side (right for hebrew, left otherwise).
Re-run on window resize, layout/setting changes, after images load and after a footnote toggle.

VERIFIED 2026-10-05 (Berakhot 2a, Hebrew, panel class `readerPanel serif hebrew continuous`): segments, their

and the rangeSpan are all display:inline. Numbers sit in the gutter just past the text on the reading-start side (x=1006 for text ending at 990) at the top of the line where their segment begins; link-count dots in the gutter on the other side (x≈258). Two segments beginning on one line (2a:3 and 2a:4): their numbers are moved by script — in the live DOM they ended at x=295 and x=284, i.e. over the text, not in the gutter (the collision fix of placeSegmentNumbers goes wrong here).

Rebuild: the segment is not positioned in continuous layout, so its absolutely positioned number and dot keep the line they would have been on (top:auto) and take their horizontal place from the surface; numbers sharing a line step outward by 20px (src/lib/reader/spread-numbers.ts) instead of landing on the text.

name: Link-count dot per segment
summary: A faint dot next to each segment shows how many connections it has.
details: linkCount > linkCountDot opacity min(count+20,70)/100; 0 when none; tooltip 'N Connections Available'.
Count respects active connections filter (Sefaria.linkCount; _filterLinks handles |Quoting and |Essay suffixes and commentary-only categories).
Hidden in heLeft/heRight, inverted in dark mode, hidden in print.
Same gutter geometry in segmented layout: number box 30px wide, 18px beyond the text end on the reading-start side at desktop width (x=1008 for text ending at 990), 16px at phone width.

name: Segment click routing
summary: Clicking different parts of a segment does different things: follow a citation, toggle a footnote, open a topic, or open connections.
details: Priority: (1) a.mutc linker debug; (2) refLink; (3) footnote sup; (4) namedEntityLink; (5) segment click -> onSegmentClick.
Segment click: TextAndConnections -> close connections; Text+multiPanel -> open/replace connections panel at n+1 (focuses new panel for a11y); Text+mobile -> TextAndConnections in-panel.
Click on a non-basetext range calls onRangeClick unless a text selection is in progress.

name: Segment keyboard accessibility
summary: Segments are keyboard focusable and openable with Enter or Space.
details: tabIndex=0, aria-label='Click to see links to <ref>', aria-describedby=panel-N, Enter/Space activation (Util.handleKeyboardClick).
Section title is .title > .titleBox[role=heading aria-level=2]; book title header role=heading level 1.

name: Highlighting of selected segment(s)
summary: The segment being studied is marked with a light-blue background — but only while the connections sidebar is open. A plain verse or range link scrolls to the verse without a visible highlight.
details: highlightedRefs explicit -> highlight those segments or all if list contains section ref/first spanning ref; otherwise basetext highlights segments flagged by makeSegments.
showHighlight toggles visible .highlight; .invisibleHighlight always set as scroll anchor. ReaderPanel showHighlight = state.showHighlight || highlightedRefs.length > 1.
CSS: .basetext .segment.highlight #F0F7FF (sepia #E3E3E1, dark #444); focus/active #f5faff.
SSR highlights segment/range URLs.
VERIFIED 2026-10-04: /Genesis.1.3 and /Genesis.1.3-5 with the sidebar closed show no .segment.highlight; with=all shows it (rgb(240,247,255)).

VERIFIED 2026-10-04: the `highlightedRefs.length > 1` branch never shows a whole range in practice — the range URL collapses to its first segment about 1s after load (TXD-055), so with the sidebar open only that first segment is highlighted.

name: Poetry line formatting
summary: Poetic texts can show each line with hanging indent.
details:
addPoetrySpans splits on
and wraps lines in span.poetry.indentWhenWrap; continuous layout neutralizes indent and hides
. CSS .indentAll, .indentAllDouble. Originally set up for the Fox translation.

DEAD: TextRange reads data.formatEnAsPoetry/formatHeAsPoetry but v3 API never sets those keys (only legacy TextFamily did); in v3 only versions[i].formatAsPoetry exists and the client ignores it. CSS and copy-cleanup remain.

name: Infinite scroll up and down in the reader
summary: Readers scroll continuously through neighboring sections without page reloads.
details: adjustInfiniteScroll: up when scrollTop < 75; down when last section bottom < viewport height + 80; handleTextLoad triggers down-only checks.
Up: prepends prev plus up to 10 earlier cached sections (buildPreviousRefs); down: appends up to 10 cached next sections. Scroll position restored after top load (restoreScrollPositionAfterTopLoad).
No adjustment while any .basetext.loading exists. Refs written via ReaderPanel.updateTextColumn (replaceHistory).
InfiniteScroll.jsx is NOT the reader's; it is the search-results loader.
Prefetch of next/prev section text with same versions.

name: Scroll container differs by device
summary: On phones the whole page scrolls; on desktop the text column scrolls.
details: Desktop (multiPanel): .textColumn scrolls. Mobile (singlePanel): window/document scrolls so browser chrome collapses.
Top threshold 140 multiPanel / 70 single in scrollToHighlighted.

Rebuild note: the old client let the browser's native scroll anchoring (overflow-anchor) run alongside its own restoreScrollPositionAfterTopLoad; the rebuild disables native anchoring and keeps the reader's place itself (TXD-068).

name: Initial and highlight scroll positioning
summary: On opening, the reader scrolls to the cited segment, leaving room above to scroll up.
details: setInitialScrollPosition: first .segment.invisibleHighlight else 90px (placeholder height).
scrollToHighlighted: top = highlighted.top + 90 + 30 - threshold; focuses highlighted segment only in last panel.
componentDidUpdate triggers: mobile connections opened; new single ref outside current refs; changed highlight; changed language/versions (no focus steal); width change restores scroll by percentage.

VERIFIED 2026-10-04: on load the old reader paints the top of the chapter first, then scrolls to the linked segment after hydration (a visible jump); the rebuild places it before first paint (TXD-068).

name: Visible-ref tracking drives URL and header
summary: As you scroll, the URL follows the segment you are reading (segment level, e.g. /Genesis.1.8), the header follows the section, and — with the sidebar open — the blue highlight and the sidebar's connections follow too (TXD-067).
details: adjustHighlightedAndVisible (debounced 100ms): first .basetext .segment whose bottom > windowMiddle (height/2, or /4 in TextAndConnections) or whose top >= threshold; in keyboard tabbing mode uses focused segment.
Sets currentlyVisibleRef (drives URL and header); sets TextList highlight (visible only with sidebar or TextAndConnections); records prevScrollPercentage.
Programmatic scroll sets justScrolled so handleScroll ignores it.
VERIFIED 2026-10-04: the URL tracks to SEGMENT level while scrolling, with or without the sidebar (/Genesis.1.3 → /Genesis.1.8). Earlier atlas wording ('the section and segment') under-stated this.

VERIFIED 2026-10-04: a section URL (/Genesis.1) stays section-level after load until the reader scrolls; a range URL (/Genesis.1.3-5) is replaced by its first segment (/Genesis.1.3) once the initial scroll settles (~1s), sidebar open or not.

Focus rule detail: positions are measured from the top of the scrolling element; threshold 140 (multi-panel) / 70 (single panel); windowMiddle = window height / 2 (or /4 in mobile TextAndConnections).

name: Loading placeholders and book title header
summary: Above and below the loaded text the column shows a book title at the start of a book or loading indicators.
details: Top: if first section has no prev -> bookMetaDataBox with book title (en/he, role=heading level 1); otherwise LoadingMessage.base.prev. Bottom: LoadingMessage.base.next if next exists, else empty .final.
Rendered only after mount to avoid SSR layout shift. Consecutive loading textRanges hidden.
TextRange with no data shows LoadingMessage ('Loading...' / hebrew) as title and .loading class.
data.error -> onTextLoad returns early; nothing rendered (no user-facing error).

name: Current-segment highlight follows the reader
summary: With the connections sidebar open, the light-blue highlight moves from segment to segment as you scroll, and the sidebar's content follows the highlighted segment.
details: VERIFIED 2026-10-04: /Genesis.1.3?with=all, scroll 400px → highlight moves to Genesis 1:8 and the URL to /Genesis.1.8; sidebar shows 1:8's connections.
Same focus rule and 100ms debounce as TXD-055 (adjustHighlightedAndVisible → setTextListHighlight). Without the sidebar the focus is tracked (URL) but not painted.
Clicking a segment makes it current (highlight + sidebar) without scrolling; it stays current until the reader scrolls.
Previously documented only as one clause inside TXD-055; split out because it is a core reading behaviour.

name: Jump-free reading: place keeping and pre-paint placement (rebuild)
summary: In the rebuild, nothing you are reading ever moves unless you scroll: sections added above, fonts arriving, the sidebar opening, font-size and layout changes all keep the current segment still, and a linked verse is in place from the first visible frame.
details: Anchor = current segment; corrections in the same task as the change (layout effect / ResizeObserver), only content shifts corrected, never the reader's own scroll.
Pre-hydration inline script positions the linked verse during HTML parsing, keeps it in place every frame until the app takes over, and holds the text invisible (≤600ms) while web fonts arrive.
The focus only moves when the reader moves, in the direction of travel (no backwards URL step near the end of a chapter).
Tested by e2e/smoothness.spec.ts (per-step jump analysis) and scripts/jank-probe.mjs.

FOUND 2026-10-07: scrolling moves in whole device pixels but text heights are fractional (22px at line-height 1.6 is 35.2px a line), so compensating a prepended section (Genesis 1 above Genesis 2:3: 3074.36px) left the verse 0.36px lower, which can paint a pixel off (e2e 'in place from the first visible frame' saw 326 → 327 at 1280px). FIXED: the engine scrolls the whole pixels and puts the remaining fraction in a sub-pixel padding above the content (kept in [0, 1)), so the verse's position is unchanged to the layout unit.

name: Neighbouring sections preloaded with the page (rebuild)
summary: The server tells the browser to fetch the previous and next sections while the app is still loading, so scrolling past an edge right after arrival is instant.
details: <link rel=preload as=fetch crossorigin> with the exact API URL the client requests (pinned by a unit test); the old client fetched neighbours only after mount.

name: Text selection and double-click guard
summary: Selecting text highlights its segments and can trigger dictionary lookup.
details: handleTextSelection on mouseup finds spanned .segments and highlights those refs; getNormalizedSelectionString removes .segmentNumber, .titleBox and hidden-language spans per panel class; calls setSelectedWords.
Mousedown with detail > 1 at a different position than last click is prevented (avoids accidental multi-click selection).
Selection color #D2DCFF.

The click that ends a drag-selection is ignored (old TextRange.handleClick: window.getSelection().type === 'Range'); the rebuild does the same in Segment. Selection text excludes segment numbers, link dots, footnote markers and bodies.

name: Copy text with clean formatting
summary: Copying text from the reader yields clean text without numbers, links or hidden-language spans.
details: Ignored for INPUT, TEXTAREA, LC-CHATBOT. Clones the selection; non-continuous: each .contentSpan becomes <div dir=rtl|ltr> (Sefaria.hebrew.isHebrew); Hebrew panel container gets dir=rtl.

name: Fonts for Hebrew, English and special scripts
summary: Text renders with fonts supporting cantillation and other scripts.
details: Serif Hebrew stack starts with 'Taamey Frank' (cantillation), Cardo (Greek), Noto Color Emoji.
English serif stack: adobe-garamond-pro, Meltho (Syriac), Crimson Text, Georgia (Cyrillic), Noto Sans Samaritan.
'Rashi Script' font face exists (sheets only).
.enInHe 83%.

VERIFIED 2026-10-05 (Chrome platform fonts via CDP): Genesis 1 Hebrew on the live site is drawn in Taamey Frank CLM (computed stack: "Noto Color Emoji", "EnglishInHebrew Serif Font", Cardo, "Taamey Frank", adobe-garamond-pro, "Crimson Text", …) — the library theme override puts the Taamey-backed face BEFORE Cardo, which also has Hebrew glyphs. English text is drawn in Adobe Garamond Pro (Adobe Fonts); a few Latin characters in Hebrew runs come from Heebo.
Citation links inside commentary (a.refLink): 0.8em of the text size, weight 700, letter-spacing 1px, colour #333, same face as the text.

Rebuild notes: a global :lang(he) rule setting the UI face also matches every descendant of a Hebrew element and silently beat the text face — fixed by making segment text and its descendants inherit. English text is Cardo (open) instead of Adobe Garamond (licensed): lines break a few words earlier; owner decision recorded in docs/PARITY_SHOTS.md.

OWNER DECISION 2026-10-06: use the legacy site's fonts. FOUND: the rebuild's stack already listed the old order ('Cardo', 'Meltho', 'adobe-garamond-pro', 'Crimson Text'…), but on sefaria.org Cardo is declared ONLY for Greek and combining marks (static/css/font-faces.css unicode-range U+0300-036F, U+0370-03FF, U+1D00-1D7F, U+1DBF, U+1F00-1FFF, U+2126, U+AB65, U+10140-1018F, U+101A0, U+1D200-1D24F); the rebuild loaded Fontsource Cardo with the full Latin range, so every English text was Cardo. Fixed: Cardo now has the legacy range (the legacy TTF), and Adobe Garamond Pro comes from Sefaria's Adobe Fonts kit `aeg8div` (the one templates/base.html loads), its regular/italic/bold woff2 preloaded so the text is in its real face at first paint (src/lib/fonts/typekit.ts, e2e/fonts.spec.ts checks the URLs against the live kit).
Deployment note: the kit's allowed-domains list (Adobe Fonts settings, owned by Sefaria) must include the host this client is served from.

name: Print stylesheet for text

decodeHebrewNumeral; encodeHebrewDaf (short '.'/':', long 'N alef/bet'); encodeHebrewFolio ('N,alef-dalet'); intToDaf, dafToInt, intToFolio.

isHebrew (majority of first 200 non-punctuation chars ignoring HTML/nikkud), containsHebrew, containsEnglish, getNikkudRegex, hebrewPlural (Daf->Dappim, Perek->Perokim, Siman->Simanim, Aliyah->Aliyot).

name: Dictionary entry rendering

details: Default headword: headword + alt_headwords comma-separated RTL.

BDB (parent_lexicon matches /^BDB.*?Dict/): markers ‡ peculiar, † all_cited, ordinal, trailing superscript digits stripped, <sub> occurrences, alt headwords with occurrences, bracket modes all/first_word, headword_suffix HTML.
Morphology (...), language_code, language_reference HTML; recursive <ol> senses: grammar (verbal_stem), definition HTML, alternative, notes, nested senses.
BDB senses: 'Note.' marker, pre_num, †, bold num+form, <sub> occurrences, definition, nested.
End notes and derivatives HTML; Attribution 'Source:' (source/source_url) and 'Creator:' (attribution/attribution_url).

Click .refLink citation -> onCitationClick + 'Citation Link Click'; click elsewhere -> onEntryClick('<lexicon index_title>, <headword>') opens dictionary entry as text + 'Click Dictionary Entry from Lookup'; Enter works.
VERIFIED 2026-10-05: line-for-line identical text on the live site and in the rebuild for בְּרֵאשִׁ֖ית, וַיֹּ֥אמֶר and אֱלֹהִ֑ים (Strong's, Jastrow, BDB).

BUG (from code, ReaderPanel-style template string in LexiconBox.renderBDBEntrySenses): `note` is a JSX element interpolated into a string, so a BDB sense with note=true would print '[object Object]' for the 'Note.' marker. The rebuild prints 'Note.'. Other old-markup problems fixed: <div> and bare <span> directly inside <ol>.

Citation links come in two forms: <a class="refLink" href data-ref> (Jastrow) and <a data-ref href> without the class (BDB). The old click handler only recognises .refLink, so BDB citations fall through to the entry click; the rebuild treats any a[data-ref] as a citation.
